reason: A ties concrete timestamps to metrics (brightness pct, CTA position, cut distribution across bins, motion mismatch between hook and body) and gives directly actionable edits, with strong insight into why the construction feels static. One minor issue is its claim of 'abrupt opening/closing cuts' when data shows 0 cuts there, but most claims check out. B's strongest point is correctly catching the spoken 'shell.apps folder' vs actual 'shell:appsFolder' mismatch (a genuinely useful accuracy insight), but several of its recommendations are generic ('add a reason to watch', 'expand CTA', 'confirm visual matches') and the 'confirm the demonstration matches' point is a non-actionable hedge about unavailable visuals. A delivers more concrete, metric-grounded, editor-ready guidance overall.
